extra.message: Student.create interpolates name into SQL using Python's % operator, then executes the resulting string without parameter binding. Unauthenticated POST /students/ passes data['name'] directly here through sqli/views.py:57. An attacker can terminate the quoted value and execute additional SQL statements.

POST /students/ creates students without checking authentication. The creation form is restricted to authenticated users in templates/students.jinja2:21, but the handler has no authorize decorator or equivalent check. Anonymous callers can bypass that restriction with a direct POST.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: POST /courses/ creates courses without checking authentication or administrator privileges. templates/courses.jinja2:25 restricts the form to administrators, but direct requests bypass that UI restriction. Anonymous users and ordinary accounts can create arbitrary courses.

POST /students/{student_id}/evaluate/{course_id} inserts grades using caller-selected student and course IDs without checking the caller's identity or administrator privileges. The administrator check exists only in templates/course.jinja2:41. An anonymous attacker can submit valid points for any existing student/course pair.

The template inserts stored student names into HTML without escaping. Anonymous POST /students/ controls these names, and sqli/app.py:35 disables autoescaping. A name containing executable HTML runs in visitors' browsers. The same name is also unescaped in templates/course.jinja2:49 and templates/evaluate.jinja2:25.

Course title and description supplied through anonymous POST /courses/ are stored and rendered as unescaped HTML. Autoescaping is disabled in sqli/app.py:35, allowing stored scripts or event handlers to execute for visitors. Other affected outputs include templates/courses.jinja2:17-18, templates/student.jinja2:19-20, and templates/review.jinja2:32.

Anonymous POST /courses/{course_id}/review stores review_text through sqli/views.py:120-129. This template renders that text without escaping, while autoescaping is disabled in sqli/app.py:35. An attacker can persist JavaScript that executes whenever another user views the course.

The evaluation handler validates the submitted form with EVALUATE_SCHEMA and returns e.as_dict() on failure at sqli/views.py:146-148. Unexpected submitted field names become validation-error keys. This template renders those keys as fieldname without escaping, and autoescaping is disabled. A crafted POST containing an HTML payload as an extra field name can execute JavaScript in the error response.

csrf_middleware is commented out of the middleware chain. Hidden _csrf_token fields are generated, but no active code verifies them or checks request origin. Cross-site form submissions can therefore trigger state changes, including login CSRF that signs a victim into an attacker-controlled account.

Successful login writes user_id into the existing anonymous Redis session without rotating its identifier. An attacker who plants a known session cookie in a victim's browser can reuse that identifier after the victim authenticates to access the authenticated session.

Passwords are verified using a single unsalted MD5 digest. migrations/001-fixtures.sql:10-13 stores passwords in this same format. Its low computational cost permits rapid offline dictionary attacks against exposed hashes, and identical passwords produce identical hashes.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: RedisStorage explicitly sets httponly=False for the authentication session cookie. JavaScript can read the session identifier through document.cookie, allowing the application's XSS vulnerabilities to steal reusable authenticated sessions.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag

extra.message: RedisStorage is constructed without enabling the session cookie's Secure flag. The cookie can consequently accompany unencrypted HTTP requests, exposing its authentication identifier to network interception. The storage constructor defaults secure to None. [Storage reference](https://aiohttp-session.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference.html)

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without Secure Attribute

extra.message: Database fixtures create accounts with hardcoded passwords, including the administrator superadmin/superadmin. Dockerfile.db:4 installs these fixtures automatically during database initialization. Anyone who knows the repository can authenticate to deployments retaining these seeded credentials.

The default configuration embeds the database credentials postgres/postgres. sqli/app.py:18 selects this configuration by default, and sqli/services/db.py:15-19 uses its credentials to connect. Deployments accepting this password expose a publicly known database credential; docker-compose.yml:9 also publishes the database port.

Every login POST performs a password check, and failure only adds an error message. Neither this handler nor the configured middleware records failed attempts, delays retries, locks accounts, or limits requests. Attackers can perform unrestricted online password guessing against known usernames.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: The HTTP application unconditionally enables debug mode. Ordinary exceptions bypass error_pages, which catches only web.HTTPException at sqli/middlewares.py:51. Requests such as POST / without username trigger an unhandled KeyError, allowing debug error responses to disclose traceback details, source locations, and internal exception messages.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The application starts an HTTP listener without TLS. The supplied configuration binds it to 0.0.0.0:8080, and docker-compose.yml:22 exposes it directly without a TLS proxy. In this supplied deployment, login passwords and session cookies traverse the network in cleartext and can be intercepted.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The anonymous review handler acquires a shared database connection before awaiting request.post(), retaining the connection while the client sends its body. No application-level body-read deadline is applied. Concurrent slow POST requests for an existing course can occupy the database pool and block database-dependent requests.
